Field `designModule.designInfo.interventionModel` changed from `PARALLEL` to `SINGLE_GROUP`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.armGroups.[0]label` changed from `Treatment with Biopsy` to `Treatment with or without Biopsy`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.armGroups.[0]description` changed from `Patients in Cohort A will undergo pre-treatment and on-treatment tumor biopsies for correlative analyses, with on-treatment biopsies obtained at cycle 3, day 1 (C3D1) +/- 3 days of treatment.` to `Participants receive combination therapy with atezolizumab, bevacizumab, and tiragolumab administered intravenously in 21-day cycles. All participants receive the same treatment regimen; assignment to Cohort A (with tumor biopsies) or Cohort B (no biopsies) does not affect treatment administration.`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.interventions.[0]type` changed from `PROCEDURE` to `DRUG`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.interventions.[0]name` changed from `Pre-Treatment Biopsy` to `Tiragolumab`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.interventions.[0]description` changed from `The pre-treatment biopsy should be performed at least 3 days prior to C1D1 of treatment.` to `Tiragolumab is a human monoclonal antibody targeting the co-inhibitory molecule and immune checkpoint inhibitor T-cell immunoreceptor with immunoglobulin (Ig) and immunoreceptor tyrosine-based inhibitory motif (ITIM) domains (TIGIT), with potential immune checkpoint inhibitory activity. This treatment may help the immune system attack cancer cells.`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.interventions.[0]armGroupLabels.[0]` changed from `Treatment with Biopsy` to `Treatment with or without Biopsy`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.interventions.[1]type` changed from `PROCEDURE` to `DRUG`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.interventions.[1]name` changed from `On-Treatment Biopsy` to `Atezolizumab`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.interventions.[1]description` changed from `While the acceptable window for the C3D1 biopsy is ±3 days, it is preferred that the biopsy occurs following all treatments on C3D1.` to `Atezolizumab is a type of targeted therapy drug called an immune checkpoint inhibitor. It is a monoclonal antibody that works by binding to the protein PD-L1 (programmed death) on the surface of some cancer cells, which keeps cancer cells from suppressing the immune system. This allows the immune system to attack and kill the cancer cells.`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.interventions.[1]armGroupLabels.[0]` changed from `Treatment with Biopsy` to `Treatment with or without Biopsy`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.interventions.[2]name` changed from `Tiragolumab` to `Bevacizumab`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.interventions.[2]description` changed from `Tiragolumab is a human monoclonal antibody targeting the co-inhibitory molecule and immune checkpoint inhibitor T-cell immunoreceptor with immunoglobulin (Ig) and immunoreceptor tyrosine-based inhibitory motif (ITIM) domains (TIGIT), with potential immune checkpoint inhibitory activity. This treatment may help the immune system attack cancer cells.` to `Bevacizumab works by blocking a protein called Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF), which some cancer cells produce in large amounts. Blocking VEGF may prevent the growth of new blood vessels that tumors need to grow, and may help improve the immune response in the tumor. Bevacizumab is a type of targeted therapy called an angiogenesis inhibitor.`
Field `armsInterventionsModule.interventions.[2]armGroupLabels.[0]` changed from `Treatment with Biopsy` to `Treatment with or without Biopsy`
Field `outcomesModule.primaryOutcomes.[0]measure` changed from `Objective Response Rate (ORR)` to `Objective Response Rate (ORR) Per RECIST v1.1`
Field `outcomesModule.primaryOutcomes.[0]description` changed from `The primary outcome of this trial is objective response rate (ORR), defined as the proportion of patients who achieve a complete or partial response to treatment according to RECIST v1.1 criteria.` to `Objective response rate (ORR) was defined as the proportion of patients whose best overall response was complete response (CR) or partial response (PR). Patients with stable disease (SD), progressive disease (PD), not evaluable (NE), or missing post-baseline response assessments were counted as non-responders.`
Field `outcomesModule.primaryOutcomes.[0]timeFrame` changed from `From time of study start to time of best response, up to 24 months` to `From screening/baseline tumor assessment through the last available tumor assessment, up to 5 months.`
Field `outcomesModule.secondaryOutcomes.[0]description` changed from `Progression free survival (PFS) measures the length of time from treatment start to disease progression or death, whichever comes first.` to `PFS was defined as the time from enrollment to the first documented disease progression or death from any cause, whichever occurred first. Patients without documented progression or death were censored at the date of their last adequate disease assessment. Per protocol, patients were followed until disease progression, death, withdrawal of consent, loss to follow-up, or study termination. Survival follow-up was conducted every 3 months (±14 days) after the Final Study/Treatment Discontinuation Visit. The study was terminated before participants reached the first prespecified survival follow-up assessment, scheduled 3 months after the Final Study/Treatment Discontinuation Visit.`
Field `outcomesModule.secondaryOutcomes.[0]timeFrame` changed from `From time of study start until disease progression or death, whichever comes first; up to 24 months` to `From enrollment to the first documented disease progression or death from any cause, whichever occurred first. Patients without documented progression or death were censored at the date of their last adequate disease assessment`
Field `outcomesModule.secondaryOutcomes.[1]description` changed from `Overall survival (OS) measures the duration of time from treatment start until death from any cause.` to `Overall survival (OS) was defined as the time from enrollment to death from any cause. Patients without a documented death were censored at their off-study date. Per protocol, patients were followed until death, withdrawal of consent, loss to follow-up, or study termination. Survival follow-up was scheduled every 3 months (±14 days) after the Final Study/Treatment Discontinuation Visit. The study was terminated before participants reached the first prespecified survival follow-up assessment, scheduled 3 months after the Final Study/Treatment Discontinuation Visit.`
Field `outcomesModule.secondaryOutcomes.[1]timeFrame` changed from `From time of study start until death by any cause, up to 24 months` to `From enrollment until death from any cause, withdrawal of consent, loss to follow-up, or study termination, with survival follow-up every 3 months (±14 days) after the Final Study/Treatment Discontinuation Visit, per protocol.`
Field `contactsLocationsModule.locations.[0]facility` changed from `Universtiy of Colorado Hospital` to `University of Colorado Hospital`
